subject: SKU allocation collar and cloud backfill plan
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: sales@zetaoem.com, partnerships@skylinecloud.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: SKU allocation collar + cloud backfill options for DL-2026-1198

Hi Maya / Zeta team / Skyline,

Quick summary: NimbusAI is asking us to commit to a 1.2M token-hour dedicated pool (approx. 40 A100-equivalent cards) starting Nov 1, but their procurement window and our OEM ETA windows aren’t lining up. We need confirmation on two fronts so we can finalize the MAP and pricing for the deal:

1) Zeta - final ETA window and whether the attached quote v3 reflects the holdback language (allocation collar) we discussed. We need a firm commitment window (earliest ship, latest ship) and any penalties or carveouts for partial shipments.
2) Skyline - confirm short-term cloud backfill capacity we can reserve for Nov->Dec, pricing delta for spot vs reserved short-term (2 month) and any minimum commitment.

What I need by EOD Thu (9/9):
- Zeta: a one-line confirmed ETA range and whether you can provide staged shipment (20/40/40) with separate serial allotments.
- Skyline: a short cost table for the two-month backfill option and a contact for a temporary PO.

If we can't get a clear ETA, my recommendation (for the MAP) is a split-delivery approach: commit to a smaller initial dedicated pool (20 cards) on Nov 1, with a pre-negotiated ladder to hit full capacity by Jan 15. That preserves the commercial commitment for Nimbus and buys us lead time.

Attachments: Zeta-quote-v3.pdf (quote, shows supply terms).

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Deals Ops, Redwood Inference


From: Zeta OEM Sales <sales@zetaoem.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SKU allocation collar + cloud backfill options for DL-2026-1198

Diego,

Thanks for the clear note. Confirming the following based on our factory schedule and freight windows:

- ETA window (firm): earliest 2026-12-18, latest 2027-01-10.
- Staged shipments: we can do staged shipments in 3 tranches (25% / 35% / 40%) but we can also do 20/40/40 if you need that split; lead time between first and second tranche is ~3 weeks, second->third ~4 weeks due to production batching.
- Allocation collar: we'll include a soft-holdback clause in the PO that guarantees OEM stock reservations for the deal but it will be subject to final payment milestones and a 5% supply tolerance.
- Penalties/carveouts: full cancellation after final PO will incur up to 10% restocking if we reallocate to other buyers; partial delays can be pushed to next production slot with a 2-4 week variance.

Attached: Zeta-quote-v3.pdf (updated with shipment split table).

Happy to jump on 30m if you want to run through specifics — mornings PST are best for our supply lead.

Regards,
Maya Suresh
Client Partnerships, Zeta OEM
Attachments: Zeta-quote-v3.pdf


From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SKU allocation collar + cloud backfill options for DL-2026-1198

Team —

FW: Maya's confirmation from Zeta above. Key takeaways and proposed approach for MAP:

- Zeta's earliest is 12/18; latest slips into Jan. That pushes full on-prem onboarding beyond Nimbus's Nov 1 target.
- We should propose a hybrid delivery in the MAP: 20-card dedicated pool on Nov 1 (hosted in Redwood Dedicated), with staggered tranche unlocks tied to milestone payments.
- For the Nov->Dec gap, Skyline can cover up to 30 A100-eq with a 2-month reserved block. Vanessa, can you confirm if Skyline's 2-month reserve would be regionally colocated and able to offer warm KV-cache replication for faster cutover? Also need the delta in unit costs vs our committed Dedicated rate.
- Laura / Karthik: commercial ask — accept lower initial capacity (20 cards) but with a clause that allows us to bill the customer pro rata or provide credit if we don't deliver full performance SLOs. This lets sales close the commitment and keeps ops protected.

Suggested next steps (quick):
1) Vanessa: get the Skyline short cost table and warm-cache feasibility by Mon EOD (9/13).
2) Laura: draft the contract clause for staged delivery and pro rata billing by Tue (9/14).
3) Karthik: estimate margin impact if we run first 2 months on Skyline reserved vs OEM delivery (rough $/token-hour delta) by Tue (9/14).

I’ll coordinate MAP language and slot the internal exec escalation if Zeta moves ETA later than 1/10.

Diego

Diego / all,

Quick update from Skyline:

- Skyline confirmed a 2-month reserved block in us-west-2 that can be instantiated Nov 1. They offered an AMI-equivalent warm image and a KV-cache sync path (cold start optimization) that reduces warmup to ~12 hours vs ~48 hours from cold. That reduces our performance gap considerably.
- Pricing: reserved 2-month block = $0.52 / token-hour (committed unit) vs spot average ~$0.30 / token-hour. Our Dedicated target rate for the customer is $0.38 / token-hour.
- Operational notes: Skyline requires a short PO and a signed SLA addendum for eviction protection; their procurement team will accept a 60% advance on the 2-month block.

Attachments: Skyline-spot-vs-reserve-costs.xlsx (cost table).

Recommendation:
- Proceed with Diego's split-delivery MAP.
- Use Skyline reserved block for Nov 1 -> Dec 31 to meet Nimbus's start date. Pass the $/token-hour delta through as a one-time infrastructure surcharge (built into a bridging credit) rather than increasing the base rate.

I’ll share the PO template and contact at Skyline in the Drive link.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Cloud Partnerships, Redwood Inference
